task_instance: Query historical Azure spend (e.g. 'show most expensive resources for the last 30 days') using the skill's documented MCP tools (query_costs, query_aks_costs, Azure Resource Graph) against a subscription.
blocker_detail: The skill's entire workflow depends on Azure-specific MCP tools named in SKILL.md (query_costs, query_aks_costs) and Azure Resource Graph queries, none of which exist in this runtime's tool list. No Azure MCP server is connected. Checked for a fallback via the Azure CLI ('az') as an alternative path to real cost data; it is not installed in this sandbox ('az: command not found'). Even if it were installed, actually retrieving real Azure Cost Management data would require an authenticated Azure subscription and credentials, which the task rules forbid using/searching for. Because the skill explicitly forbids transforming or fabricating cost data outside the MCP tool ('Never transform MCP results in a shell or interpreter; request tool-side totals...'), there is no way to produce a genuine deliverable (an actual cost breakdown/spike analysis) without the missing tool and account access. The skill source directory also contains no reference workflow files (only SKILL.md and LICENSE), reinforcing that it is designed purely as a thin wrapper around a provided Azure MCP integration.
evidence: Read SKILL.md (references query_costs, query_aks_costs, Resource Graph MCP tools). Listed skill source directory: only SKILL.md and LICENSE present, no workflow reference docs to inspect further, no sample data included. Ran `which az` and `az --version` and `az account show` in the work directory: all failed with 'az: command not found' (exit 127), confirming no Azure tooling or CLI is present. No Azure MCP tool appears anywhere in the available/deferred tool lists for this session. No credentials, subscription, or Azure account exist or may be used in this sandbox per the safety rules, so the core deliverable (a real, verified Azure cost analysis) cannot be produced or even attempted with mock substitutes without violating the skill's own instruction against fabricating/transforming results outside the designated tool.
